title: Robot Test Wizard — Grounded AI-Driven Test Automation Framework
description: A **cloud-ready, data-driven test automation framework** built on Robot Framework 7.x and Playwright, where AI coding agents generate modern, hallucination-free test code grounded in dynamically reflected, version-locked library documentation (LEGO Architecture: code, YAML test data, env config, and masked secrets strictly separated).
fullDescription:
**Robot Test Wizard** rethinks test automation for the agent era: instead of letting LLMs hallucinate deprecated Robot Framework 3/4 syntax, the framework **grounds AI coding agents in their exact installed environment**.

**Grounded AI generation (`tools/dump_libdocs.py`)** — runs Robot Framework's native `robot.libdoc` introspection against the precise library binaries in the active virtualenv (RF 7.x `VAR`/`RETURN`/`TRY EXCEPT`/`Secret`, Playwright Browser Library, RequestsLibrary, plus custom libraries) and compiles them into human-readable `docs/robot-libraries/*.md`, a `KEYWORDS_QUICKREF.md` index, and a `.agents/skills/robotframework-architect` skill (SKILL.md + reference mirrors) that coding agents like Antigravity/GitHub Copilot read before generating a single keyword — auditable via conversation transcripts.

**LEGO Architecture** — `.robot` files are pure workflow orchestration with zero hardcoded data. All scenarios live in `resources/config/testdata/*.yaml` (e.g. single product, multi-product bundle, quantity duplication, negative catalog tests), environment parameters in `environments/<env>/env.yaml`, and user personas in `users.yaml`. A `DataLoader` pre-run `SuiteVisitor` AST modifier dynamically clones test cases per YAML scenario and injects environment config.

**Zero-cleartext secrets** — credentials are never committed: `users.yaml` stores pointers (`secret_env`) to git-ignored `.env`, and `DataLoader` wraps them in `robot.api.types.Secret` so execution reports log strictly `<secret>`.

**Structured PDF verification** — receipts downloaded during checkout are parsed from binary PDF streams into semantic XML via `pypdf`, then asserted with Robot Framework's XML library and **XPath** on line items and grand totals.

**Fast-fail & graceful negative handling** — catalog existence is validated with `Browser.Get Element Count` (fails in 0s with a clean business error), while `TRY ... EXCEPT`-wrapped keywords validate expected YAML-defined error messages and conclude with `Pass Execution`.

**Closed-loop `--dryrun` sandbox** — a zero-side-effect Robot Framework `--dryrun` acts as a ~3s semantic compiler for any agent-generated suite (keywords exist, argument types match, IF/TRY/FOR/WHILE block boundaries valid, YAML binds correctly), enabling an automated self-healing loop that only ships compilable tests.

**Playwright vs. Selenium evaluation** — documented engineering comparison (in-process CDP WebSocket vs. HTTP JSON Wire, zero driver hell, native auto-waiting, strict-mode locators, network mocking, multi-engine Chromium/Firefox/WebKit coverage on Windows). Packaged with a Streamlit install-wizard and PowerShell/Batch quick runners.

title: Music Note Reader — Precision Neural OMR & Audio Player
description: A **100% local, zero-API-key** Optical Music Recognition system and interactive web player: upload a scanned sheet or PDF and get editable **MusicXML**, playable **multi-instrument WAV / MIDI** — every note, key signature and rhythm transcribed by a hybrid SegNet + Transformer neural pipeline.
fullDescription:
**Music Note Reader** converts scanned sheet music and PDF documents into editable **MusicXML**, playable multi-instrument polyphonic audio (WAV), and **Standard MIDI** — with zero cloud dependencies and no API keys.

**Precision Neural OMR (TrOMR + SegNet)** — powered by `homr`'s hybrid SegNet staff/symbol segmentation and Transformer-based end-to-end sequence recognition, resolving key signatures, time signatures, clefs, notes, accidentals, ties, rests, and measures with pitch & rhythm accuracy.

**Original sheet layout preservation** — the engine keeps the printed system breaks and measure-per-row layout (`<print new-system="yes"/>`), so the rendered score mirrors the source page exactly.

**Multi-instrument audio synthesis** — a built-in additive synthesizer with instrument-specific ADSR envelope modeling: 🎹 acoustic grand piano (hammer-strike percussive decay), ⛪ pipe/church organ (multi-rank harmonic plenum), 🎻 string ensemble (vibrato sawtooth), 🪈 concert flute (breathy woodwind), ⚡ electric piano (Rhodes bell-tine), ✨ music box/celesta (inharmonic chimes), and 👾 8-bit chiptune square waves.

**Multi-format input & async pipeline** — PDFs rendered to crisp 300-DPI via `pypdfium2` (no external Poppler), plus PNG/JPG/WEBP uploads, with real-time 0–100% progress reporting across segmentation, dewarping, transformer inference, and synthesis stages.

**Interactive vector engraving** — [OpenSheetMusicDisplay](https://opensheetmusicdisplay.org/) renders the MusicXML as interactive zoomable SVG with one-click downloads of WAV, MIDI, and MusicXML. FastAPI backend + async job worker, deployed as a Dockerized Cloud Run service.

title: Testing New Models — Frontier AI Spatial Reasoning Benchmark
description: A comparative benchmark suite evaluating **Gemini 4**, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen 3.8 Max and Kimi 3 on hard spatial-reasoning tasks: programmatic vector generation (SVG), animation mechanics, and an interactive **3D Jenga physics tower**.
fullDescription:
**Frontier AI Model Benchmark Suite** independently probes the latest frontier LLMs with three escalating spatial challenges.

**The pelican-on-a-bicycle benchmark** — popularised by Simon Willison — exposes a model's internal world model: it must compose a rigid mechanical bicycle (matched wheel radii, closed diamond frame, handlebars, pedals) with organic pelican anatomy (webbed feet on pedals, wings on the bars) in a coherent Cartesian coordinate system it cannot see.

**The toad & fly test** — spatial-temporal coordination: the fly buzzes a dynamic path while the toad's eyes track it, and the tongue strike projects to exact coordinates with contact adhesion and retraction.

**Gemini 4's Jenga Tower** — the standout artifact under `gemini-4/`: a true WebGL/Three.js 3D scene with OrbitControls, directional lighting, and wooden-block texturing; rigid-body physics via Cannon.js (collision bounds, friction, mass distribution, collapse dynamics); and real-time structural load analysis telling which blocks are safe to extract.

Models are ranked chronologically by release: Gemini 4 (Sep 30 — Oct 13, 2026), DeepSeek-V4 (Jul 31 — Oct 17), Qwen 3.8 Max (Jul 19 — Aug 3), Kimi 3 (Jul 16 — 27).

**Try the live demo** — the Jenga tower simulator runs fully in the browser.

title: GrantLoom — AI Grant Intelligence & Compliance Appliance
description: A **self-hosted RAG appliance** for academic research labs: cross-references grant solicitations against institutional documents and answers with citations that resolve to **file, page, line, sheet and row** coordinates. Four LLM-judged guardrail gates (G1–G4), a bounded rewrite loop with explicit *unverified* warnings, compliance matrix with Satisfied/Partial/Gap evidence, and a golden-set evaluation harness that reports its own measurement caveats.
fullDescription:
**GrantLoom** weaves funding solicitations and lab documents into verifiable answers. Ingestion runs through an async SQLite outbox (extract → chunk → two-tier injection scan → embed → index into ChromaDB vectors, FTS5 keywords, spreadsheet tables and a KùzuDB knowledge graph), with content-hash dedup, versioning, quarantine and a deletion saga that purges every store.

Questions flow through a single agent pipeline — **Planner → Retriever → Writer → Validator** — streamed as SSE. The writer only emits `[chunk_id]` markers; the backend resolves them to physical coordinates and an **independent judge model** (different family, NFR-6) verifies every claim against its cited evidence, driving a bounded rewrite loop. Retrieval fuses dense + BM25 (RRF) with two extra tools: LLM-written SQL over spreadsheet schemas (AST-guarded, results become citable chunks) and graph traversal over extracted entities.

The decision layer is a typed **DecisionBackendPort**: a prompt-based LLM judge primary with a labelled, metered heuristic fallback — degradation is never silent. Deployment is a multi-stage Docker image (non-root, ~230 MB RSS) behind nginx with TLS, unbuffered SSE and per-IP rate limiting, running in **public BYOK mode**: zero server-side secrets — every visitor's inference runs on their own live-probed OpenRouter key (deepseek-v4-flash writer, gpt-4o-mini judge). Prometheus scrapes custom gate/tool/ingestion metrics.

title: Latch — Zero-Trust Neural PII Pre-Commit Guardrail
description: A **100% local, CPU-native git pre-commit hook** running the ultra-compact **Julia-1 (144M)** decision model to block leaked PII and credentials before they ever leave the laptop — 0% FNR on real secrets, single-digit-ms warm daemon latency, and a live **Prometheus + Grafana** observability stack.
fullDescription:
**Latch** (pii-guardrail) is an ultra-fast, 100% local git pre-commit guardrail powered by **Julia-1** — a 144.3M-parameter non-autoregressive decision model built on `mmBERT-small` — that blocks PII (names+phones, addresses, government IDs) and leaked credentials (API keys, tokens, DB passwords) before code leaves the developer's machine.

**Why it's different:** Classic tools rely on rigid regex rules that miss natural-language semantic leaks, while cloud LLMs violate privacy and add multi-second commit latency. Latch runs entirely on the local CPU: zero cloud calls, zero telemetry, zero data exfiltration.

**Architecture highlights:**
- **Warm daemon + client** — a loopback HTTP daemon keeps Julia-1 warm (~50ms probe), with seamless in-process cold-start fallback; token-authenticated telemetry endpoints (`/metrics` Prometheus, `/v1/stats` JSON, protected web dashboard)
- **Fail-closed invariant** — missing weights, corrupt tensors, diff-parse failures, or crashes **always abort the commit** with actionable diagnostics (test suite: `test_fail_closed.py`)
- **Dissection pinpointing** — flags the exact lines and classifications in a diff, not just 'this file is bad'
- **Adversarial hardening** — prompt-injection resistance at 100% injection resilience, per-file batching partition, sliding-window chunk overlap against boundary PII
- **91-test suite** — unit tests + live Julia-1 integration, benchmark gates FNR at 0.0%

**Benchmark (CPU):** FNR 0.0% (zero missed leaks), FPR 14.3%, injection resilience 100%, mean warm-daemon latency ~1.2s/sample forward pass (forward_ms = 99.5%+ of phase time).

**Observability:** a running **Prometheus → Grafana** stack visualizes throughput, token counts, phase-by-phase latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99), cache hit/miss, and CPU/RSS saturation — dashboards live while the test suite runs.

**🎬 Hackathon demo video (silent, 3:00):** [portfolio.taskmind-ai.com/pii-guardrail-demo.mp4](https://portfolio.taskmind-ai.com/pii-guardrail-demo.mp4) — opens with the README (problem → solution), then shows Latch **blocking** a commit containing real PII (Jane Doe + sk-live token), the remediated env-var version being **accepted** (`✓ Latch: Clean (daemon)`), and closes on the **live Grafana dashboard** while tests run — throughput, token counts, and phase-latency percentiles from the Prometheus stack.

**🎙️ Narration:** The 3-minute walkthrough is now produced by **Frame Talk** — the multimodal screen-to-podcast studio engine. Hosts **Alex** (Lead Systems Architect) and **Sarah** (Dev Advocate) deliver a synchronized two-host technical podcast anchored to the actual video frames (Gemini 3.7 Flash vision + Chronos timeline holds). [▶ Watch the narrated version](https://portfolio.taskmind-ai.com/pii-guardrail-demo-podcast.mp4) (click Play on the card — the in-page player opens; the file also downloads 7.7MB MP4, H.264+AAC 24kHz)

**🏆 Hackathon:** Submitted to the [Devpost AI Hackathon — Latch](https://devpost.com/software/latch-8cknvz).

title: JobAgent — Autonomous Career CRM & Statutory Compliance Engine
description: A **local-first, autonomous career dashboard** that turns chaotic job hunting into a single intelligent cockpit: 1-click posting archive with Markdown + PDF snapshots, multi-protocol email triage with genuine **interview detection** (even in German), and automatic **Agentur für Arbeit** proof reports. Built on the **AWS Strands Agents SDK** — zero PII leaves your machine.
fullDescription:
**JobAgent** is an autonomous background agent for job seekers, submitted to the **Agents for Humans** hackathon (AWS Strands Agents SDK). It turns the chaos of job hunting — expiring postings, scattered emails, hidden interview invites — into a single intelligent cockpit with zero PII leaving the machine.

**What it does:**
- **Dual-asset archiving** — 1-click browser extension captures a clean Markdown brief *and* a pixel-perfect PDF snapshot before the posting disappears
- **3-tier email triage** — deterministic rules → offline ML classifier → Gemini semantic reasoning detects genuine interview invitations (including German 'Einladung zum Vorstellungsgespräch'), filters recruiter spam/webinars, tracks Applied → Interview → Rejected lifecycles
- **Statutory compliance** — automatically compiles the official German **Agentur für Arbeit** proof table (*Eigenbemühungsnachweis*, §138 SGB III) as print-ready PDF
- **Agent-to-Agent (A2A) & MCP server** — Telegram, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other parent agents query and control JobAgent via standard A2A/SSE endpoints
- **100% local-first** — SQLite CRM + local archive; optional Ollama for true zero-cloud inference

**Architecture:** Strands Agent Coordinator (Gemini) orchestrating EmailIngestTool → JobArchiveTool → ReportRenderTool over a local SQLite CRM, exposed via FastAPI A2A gateway + MCP and a Chrome Manifest V3 Copilot extension.

**Quality:** 49-test suite (PII/secret scans clean across full git history), adversarial QA pass, DNS-rebinding-guarded loopback gateway.

Demo video (2:02, narrated): screencast replayed with Frame Talk's synchronized two-host walkthrough. Code: https://github.com/tdk67/jobagent

title: Frame Talk — Multimodal Screen-to-Podcast Studio Engine
description: Transforms silent developer screencasts and README docs into synchronized **two-host technical podcast** walkthroughs — **Gemini 3.7 Flash** vision reads video pixels, **Chronos Sync Engine** matches dialogue to UI actions with millisecond precision.
fullDescription:
**Frame Talk** is the Multimodal Screen-to-Podcast Studio Engine, built for the Agentic Cinema Hackathon. It ingests a raw silent `.mp4` screencast plus project `README.md`, and uses **Gemini 3.7 Flash** native multimodal comprehension to extract granular visual scenes (UI actions, clicks, terminal logs, state transitions) directly from video pixels — no external transcripts.

**Pipeline:** Ingestion & Alignment Agent → Scriptwriter Persona Agent → QA & Pacing Audit Agent → Chronos Sync Engine (TTS + duration meter + freeze calculator) → Compiler Agent (FFmpeg 1080p stitching with permanent holds).

**Highlights:**
- Scriptwriter persona agents generate organic two-host dialogue between *Mark (Lead Systems Architect)* and *Sarah (Dev Advocate)* with natural turn-taking pauses (180-240ms) and zero synthetic timestamps.
- **Chronos Sync Engine** synthesizes every line via `gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` at 24kHz PCM, measuring audio duration to the millisecond (`duration_ms = pcm_bytes / 48`) and computing `required_freeze_ms` to hold the video timeline at the focal action — audio and screen never desync.
- Observability via **ClickHouse** time-series DB + **Grafana** dashboard tracking `turn_index`, `audio_ms`, `freeze_ms`, and drift.
- **BYOK** — no server-side credentials required.

title: Idea Lint — Adversarial Multi-Agent Venture Validation Engine (FlyRank Capstone)
description: An impartial **AI courtroom for startup ideas** — researches with live Google Search grounding, debates across adversarial agents, and outputs an audit-proof, scored PRD. Privacy-first with zero cloud storage and **BYOK** free-tier support. Google hackathon submission: [devpost.com/software/idea-lint](https://devpost.com/software/idea-lint)
fullDescription:
**Idea Lint** (formerly VentureBot) is an adversarial, multi-agent venture validation engine built on **Google ADK**. It takes a raw startup concept and runs it through a panel of specialized agents with deliberately asymmetric information access:

- **Researcher** — mines competitor signals and market metrics via live Google Search grounding
- **Creative Ideator** — proposes lateral pivot angles
- **Advocate** — argues the strongest bull case
- **Critic** — red-teams feasibility, moats, and unit economics traps
- **Judge** — synthesizes everything into structured 1-10 scores (Novelty, Feasibility, Market Fit) with a PROCEED / PARK / PRUNE verdict
- **PRD Writer + Security Auditor** — produce a rigorous, machine-actionable PRD

V1 was submitted to the **Google Gemini Hackathon** on Devpost: https://devpost.com/software/idea-lint. For the FlyRank Backend Track Capstone it was re-architected into a production-grade, **zero-retention backend**: decoupled asynchronous job engine, hardened REST gateway with rate limiting, adversarial agent guardrails, a **161-test** deterministic test suite, and browser-local IndexedDB persistence (BYOK). Live demo: https://idea-lint.taskmind-ai.com

title: 3D Quaternion Calculator
description: Interactive **3D wireframe cube** calculator powered by quaternion rotation — with an exact **rational-number calculator** side-by-side.
fullDescription:
A **dual-mode interactive calculator** built with Python and Streamlit.

- **Rational Mode** — exact arithmetic using Python's `fractions.Fraction` class; no floating-point errors (`1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2`, not `0.4999...`)
- **Quaternion Mode** — live 3D wireframe cube with RGB coordinate axes, rotated via a calculator-style numpad with real-time perspective projection; scientific degree input for precise pitch / yaw / roll

Originally created as an **AI pair-programming experiment** to test how well an AI assistant could design an interactive calculator with exact fraction arithmetic and 4D quaternion math — the 3D viewport demonstrates quaternion operations visually, no game engine required.

title: kt-puml — Kotlin PlantUML CLI
description: Blazingly fast CLI that generates **PlantUML & Mermaid sequence diagrams** from Spring Boot Kotlin source via **AST parsing** — not LLM hallucination.
fullDescription:
A **deterministic code-to-diagram generator** for Kotlin / Spring Boot codebases using **Tree-sitter AST parsing** to extract real runtime call chains — no dynamic tracing, no LLM guessing.

**Features:**
- Hybrid discovery (OS grep for endpoints + file walker for class indexing)
- JIT parsing with two-tier cache (85ms per endpoint)
- Scope-aware type resolution for constructor / property injection
- Dynamic adapter resolution with `typeHints`
- Conditional block rendering (`opt` / `else` / `end`), call tree de-duplication, chain-call cleanup (collapsing builder patterns like `webClient`)

Outputs **PlantUML (`.puml`)**, **Mermaid (`.mmd`)**, and SVG, plus an interactive HTML dashboard with searchable diagrams. Zero global config — just a `.kt-puml.json` in your project root. Built for CI/CD pipelines and large enterprise codebases.

title: Pi A2A Agent Mesh

fullDescription:

description: Production-grade **3-stage ETL web scraper** with politeness ethics layer and Streamlit live demo, deployed on Streamlit Community Cloud.

title: BE-07 — Book Translation API with LLM
description: Production-grade **schema-validated translation API** with 5-layer prompt injection defense, cost logging, kill switch, and Swagger UI — deployed on a VPS behind Nginx.
fullDescription:
A **production-grade, schema-validated API** that accepts a book ID and target language (`de/fr/it/en`), fetches a scraped book record, and uses an LLM (via OpenRouter) to generate clean, structured JSON translations of the book's title and description.

**Built with** FastAPI + the official OpenAI client library — provider-agnostic (local Ollama or cloud OpenRouter).

**Features:**
- Strict **Pydantic validation** (`extra=forbid`, `min_length=1`)
- Response match verification + 1 repair retry on schema failure with quarantine logging
- 30s cumulative wall-clock timeout (HTTP 504) and exponential backoff on rate limits
- Structured cost logging to JSONL
- **Fail-closed Kill Switch** (`LLM_ENABLED=false` → HTTP 503)

**Security:** 5-Layer Prompt Injection Defense (OWASP LLM01) — role separation, JSON encoding, anti-hijacking instructions, hard schema firewall, and few-shot security examples — preventing scraped text from hijacking prompt instructions.

Deployed on a VPS behind Nginx reverse proxy with Let's Encrypt SSL. **15 passing pytest tests**, a 9-case eval suite (100% pass rate), and interactive Swagger UI docs.

title: BE-08 — PDF Report Generator & Immediate Streaming API
description: Executive analytics & branded **PDF reporting engine** with single-flight concurrency, idempotency, and an immediate **0ms-TTFB streaming endpoint** — deployed on a VPS behind Nginx.
fullDescription:
An **executive analytics and PDF reporting engine** for the FlyRank Backend Track. Queries the BE-06-Scraper SQLite database (1,000 books), generates **FL-05 Identity Kit-branded PDF reports** (Inter & JetBrains Mono, Sky Blue `#0284c7`), served via two modes:

- **Standard endpoint** (`POST /reports`) — returns a file link
- **Immediate streaming endpoint** (`POST /reports/stream`) — streams PDF bytes in 8KB chunks straight from memory/disk with **0ms TTFB** on idempotent hits

**Architecture highlights:**
- Clean 4-layer separation (routers → services → repository → SQLite, zero SQL outside the repository layer)
- **Single-Flight** `asyncio.Lock` with double-check pattern preventing races under concurrent generation
- **Same-day idempotency** — duplicate requests reuse the existing PDF
- SQL aggregations computed directly in SQLite with performance indexes (`idx_books_category/rating/price`)
- Configurable catalog cap (`max_catalog_limit`) with truncation badge
- **Jinja2 template decoupling** — design changes require zero backend edits
- **Playwright headless Chromium** rendering to pixel-perfect A4 bytes, isolated in a thread-pool executor

Includes a live streaming monitor dashboard (`GET /demo`) with real-time ReadableStream reading, live TTFB and chunk counters. **23 passing pytest tests** across 6 modules including a 5-request concurrency test. Deployed on a VPS behind Nginx + Let's Encrypt SSL — live demo: https://taskmind-ai.com/flyrank-be-08/demo

description: An autonomous **Agentic GraphRAG engine** for sovereign AI data-center supply chains: unifies a **332-node NetworkX knowledge graph**, **ChromaDB sovereign-contract vectors**, and a **SQLite BOM/PO SSOT** behind a 6-pattern adaptive intent router, prompt-injection guardrails, ABAC persona clearance, and zero-hallucination citations.
fullDescription:
**Aethelgard Infra-GraphRAG** (rag6-supply-chain) is a tri-modal sovereign infrastructure & supply-chain intelligence engine that answers operational, legal, and financial questions about AI data-center hardware supply chains — from a Streamlit showcase with 4 workspaces:

**Stack:** Python 3.11, Streamlit, ChromaDB (BGE small embeddings), NetworkX, SQLite SSOT, PyMuPDF, OpenRouter adapter, hexagonal ports & DI registry.

**Validation:** 27/27 pytest suite + 10/10 benchmark RAG queries (faithfulness 0.94, correctness 1.00, citation accuracy 1.00). Hosted on Streamlit Cloud; fully containerized with Docker for self-hosting.

title: Song Blueprint Analyzer — Music Analyzer
description: **Serverless, client-side music analyzer**: upload an MP3/WAV and get a structured musicological blueprint — local Web Audio DSP tempo estimation plus a multimodal LLM (BYOK via OpenRouter) that identifies key, BPM, genre, instruments, song structure and synced lyrics with an interactive energy timeline.
fullDescription:
**Song Blueprint Analyzer** turns a raw audio file into a complete, structured musicological breakdown — entirely in the browser, with zero server-side storage.

Local DSP first: the audio is decoded client-side with the Web Audio API into PCM buffers, low-pass filtered at 150 Hz to isolate the kick, and peak-to-peak interval analysis estimates the BPM instantly. The track is then base64-encoded and sent to a multimodal LLM (e.g. `google/gemini-3.5-flash`) via OpenRouter using the `input_audio` block type — the model "hears" the track to identify the key, refine the BPM, tag genres, map dominant instruments, segment structural boundaries (Intro → Verse → Chorus → Bridge → Outro), transcribe time-synced lyrics, and output a dynamic energy timeline.

A strict JSON schema with defensive parsing (markdown-wrap cleanup) populates interactive visual panels; clicking a lyric line or song-map section jumps the playhead to the exact timestamp on a WaveSurfer.js timeline, with a Recharts energy-over-time area chart. Bring-Your-Own-Key OpenRouter integration means no API keys are stored anywhere. React 19 + Vite + TypeScript, vanilla CSS cyber-dark UI.
